newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - June 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Wachovia Corp ha agreed to acquire Central Fidelity Banks Inc for about $2.3 billion in a stock exchange.

* Two competing bills in the U.S. House and Senate would allow the television industry to keep indefinitely the additional channel capacity from digital television, while possibly delaying the introduction of HDTV.
* Civil rights leader Andrew Young issued a report saying an investigation has found no evidence of labor abuses by Nike in Asia.
* The U.S. House of Representatives rejected a proposal to end China's normal trading status with the United States.
* Netscape Communications Corp and Microsoft have received U.S. government permission to export Internet software that uses security technology.
* The index of consumer confidence reached its highest level in 28 years, according to the business research group Conference Board.
* UtiliCorp United Inc and PECO Energy Co are banding together with AT&T Corp to offer a one-stop shopping service for a variety of utilities.
* State attorneys general defended the settlement with the tobacco industry, rebutting critics who contend it was too lenient on cigarette makers.
* Bank of Nova Scotia has agreed to acquire National Trustco Inc for $900 million.
* The ABC television network has named Stu Bloomberg chairman of its entertainment division.
* Edmund Jenkins, the former managing director of Arthur Andersen, has been named the new chairman of the Financial Accounting Standards Board.
* Conservation Corp of Africa is drawing rich eco-tourists to Africa.
* Market Place: Hong Kong's stock market, defying even the most optimistic forecasters, is reacting favorably in the months leading up to the handover from Britain to communist China.
* Philip Morris Cos is expected to provide the majority of the initial $10 billion payment called for under the recent settlement reached with plaintiffs' lawyers and state attorneys general.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rebounded Tuesday, gaining 153.80 points to close at 7758.06, after plunging Monday over concerns about comments made by Japan Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
